transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

I guess what finally made me come in is how tense my body feels all the time. My neck and shoulders are tight, and even my jaw—like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV at night.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there’s no immediate reason to be concerned?

Yes, I do. It kind of jumps around—one minute I’m worrying the contractors missed something with the house, then I’m thinking my lesson plans aren’t good enough, or the robotics kids are falling behind. And then it turns into worrying I’m letting my wife or family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms that also feel out of your control, like stomach issues, headaches, or dizziness, even when there's no clear reason for them?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like dizziness in particular, and I can’t say there’s a clear stomach thing or headaches that stand out. It’s more that I feel wound up, but I don’t know about those other symptoms.
Do you find it hard to stop worrying once it starts, even when you try to distract yourself or focus on something else?

Yes. That’s actually one of the hardest parts. I can tell myself, “Stop, focus on the class in front of you,” but then one small thing pops up—like a late invoice or a student falling behind—and it turns into a whole chain of what-ifs. Once it starts, I have a really hard time shutting it off.
Do you find it hard to relax or feel restless, like you can't sit still or settle down, even when there's no specific reason to worry?

Yes, I do. I feel wound up most of the day, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong. Even between classes I’ll catch myself pacing around the room, or checking my phone for messages from the contractor when there’s no real reason to keep looking. It’s hard to just sit and settle down.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual or that you’re running out of energy easily, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Yes, definitely. By the time the last bell rings, I feel completely wrung out. And it’s not just normal tiredness—getting a decent night’s sleep or having a quiet Sunday doesn’t really seem to reset me. Even something simple like grading a short stack of quizzes can feel like I’m pushing through mud.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, like your heart races, you can't catch your breath, or you feel like something terrible is about to happen?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I do feel worried a lot, but I can’t really think of sudden episodes where it hits all at once like that, with my heart racing or feeling like something terrible is about to happen. It’s more constant than sudden, I guess.
Have you noticed that you have trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks because your mind keeps jumping to worries or concerns?

Yes, that happens a lot. I’ll try to focus on the lesson or on marking work, and then one thought pops in—like a late invoice or a student who’s falling behind—and suddenly I’m running through all these what-ifs. I can tell myself to stop and get back to what I’m doing, but it doesn’t really switch off easily.
Have you noticed that you're more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even over small things that wouldn't usually bother you?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed being especially irritable, at least not in a way that stands out. I mean, everyone gets annoyed sometimes, but I wouldn’t say that’s been a main thing for me lately.
Have you noticed any trouble with your sleep, like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrested, even when you’re physically tired?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear sleep problem as such. Some nights I might take a bit longer to settle, but I wouldn’t say it’s been a major thing or something I’ve been tracking.
Do you find that your worries tend to jump around between many different things, even small ones, or do they usually center around a few specific concerns?

It definitely jumps around. It’s not just one big worry. I’ll start thinking, did the contractors miss something in the house, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether my lesson plans are falling behind, or the robotics students aren’t keeping up. Then it turns into whether I’m letting my wife or the family down because I’m not keeping everything under control. It can be small things, but they build quickly.
Would you say that you experience worry about a number of everyday things—like work, family, or minor issues—on most days, and that this has been going on for several months or longer?

Yes, I’d say so. It’s most days. My mind just keeps moving from one thing to the next—like whether the contractors missed something at the house, then whether my lesson plans are slipping, then whether the robotics kids are falling behind. And then I start worrying I’m disappointing my wife or the family because I’m not keeping everything under control. It’s been going on for quite a while, more than just a few weeks.
Do you often experience muscle tension, such as tightness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw, even when you’re not actively doing something stressful?

Yes. That’s actually one of the things that finally pushed me to come in. My neck and shoulders are tight almost all the time now, and I notice my jaw clenched too. It feels like I’m bracing for bad news, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or watching TV at night.
Do you find that your anxiety or worry is spread across many different events or activities, rather than just focusing on one or two specific things?

Yes, it’s definitely spread out. I don’t stay on just one thing. My mind goes from the house and whether the contractors missed something, to school stuff like lesson plans, to whether the robotics students are falling behind. Then I start worrying I’m letting my wife or my family down because I’m not keeping everything under control.
Would you say that your worry feels uncontrollable, like you can’t manage or reduce it even when you try?

Yes. I try to tell myself, “Just stop and focus on the class in front of you,” but it doesn’t really work. One small thing, like remembering a late invoice or thinking a student might be falling behind, can set off this whole chain of what-ifs. And once it starts, I have a hard time shutting it down.
Would you say these worries and the way you're feeling are causing you significant distress or making it harder for you to function in your job, relationships, or other areas of your life?

Yes, it is. I’ve started falling behind on lesson prep and grading, which isn’t like me. And outside of work, I had to give up some of the community-theater work I usually help manage because I just couldn’t keep up with all of it anymore. It’s frustrating.
